lines.text: I have measured out my life with coffee spoons.
lines.src: The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock, 1915

lines.text: Hope is the thing with feathers that perches in the soul.
Do I dare disturb the universe?
The fog comes on little cat feet.
Tell all the truth but tell it slant.
Because I could not stop for Death, he kindly stopped for me.
Two roads diverged in a wood, and I took the one less traveled by.
The woods are lovely, dark and deep, but I have promises to keep.
lines.src: Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening, 1923

lines.text: Nature's first green is gold, her hardest hue to hold.
Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?
Season of mists and mellow fruitfulness.
Things fall apart; the centre cannot hold.
Attention is the beginning of devotion.
